subject: Literature
title: French Naturalism and Zola's Experiment
description: A quick, practical guide to French Naturalism and Zola's Experiment.

hook.text: Émile Zola believed novelists should study humans like scientists study lab specimens, without sentiment.

buildup.text: Naturalism pushed realism further by showing how heredity, environment, and instinct determined human fate.

discovery.text: Zola wrote twenty novels tracking one family through addiction, poverty, madness, and political upheaval.

twist.text: Critics attacked naturalism as ugly and immoral, but Zola argued literature must show life without cosmetics.

climax.text: Naturalism influenced writers worldwide and laid the groundwork for gritty modern realism in fiction and film.

punchline.text: Zola turned the novel into a laboratory of human nature.

quiz.question: How did naturalism differ from realism?
options: Naturalism emphasized heredity, environment, and instinct as deterministic forces
